terms.meaning: A current in a wire produces a magnetic field around it.
A current-carrying coil that behaves as a magnet.
A conductor produces heat when current flows through it.
The two plates of different metals in a cell.
The liquid or paste in a cell that reacts with the electrodes.
An alloy used as heating wire, because it gets very hot when current flows.

items.name: Oersted’s discovery
items.formula: A compass needle moves when current flows in a wire nearby, and goes back when it stops.
items.example: The needle turns as soon as the switch is ON.

items.name: Making an electromagnet stronger
items.formula: More current, more turns of wire, and an iron core.
items.example: A coil with an iron nail attracts many more paper clips.

items.name: Poles of an electromagnet
items.formula: Reversing the current swaps the north and south poles.
items.example: Swap the battery connections and a compass needle swings the other way.

items.name: Uses of electromagnets
items.formula: They can be switched on and off.
items.example: Cranes lift scrap iron with the current ON and drop it when OFF. Electric bells use them too.

items.name: Earth’s magnetic field
items.formula: Comes from moving liquid iron in the outer core.
items.example: It shields us from harmful particles from space and guides some migrating birds.

items.name: What changes the heat
items.formula: Material, thickness and length of the wire, the current, and how long it flows.
items.example: Two cells warm a wire more than one cell.

items.name: Appliances that use heating
items.formula: Electric iron, room heater, kettle, geyser and hair dryer.
items.example: An incandescent bulb glows because its filament gets very hot.

items.name: Danger of overheating
items.formula: It can melt plastic parts and start fires. Safety devices in house circuits reduce this.
items.example: Use wires of the right rating.

items.name: Voltaic cell
items.formula: Two different metals in an electrolyte: a chemical reaction gives current.
items.example: Zinc and copper in lemon juice can light an LED.

items.name: Galvani and Volta
items.formula: Galvani saw a dead frog’s leg kick. Volta showed that the current came from the metals and the liquid.
items.example: The cell is named after them.

items.name: Dry cell
items.formula: The electrolyte is a moist paste. Zinc case: negative. Carbon rod: positive.
items.example: It does not spill, so it is easy to carry.

items.name: Rechargeable batteries
items.formula: A current from outside reverses the chemical reactions, so they can be used again.
items.example: Lithium-ion batteries in phones and lead-acid batteries in cars.

items.name: Throwing away batteries
items.formula: Used batteries harm the environment, so they should be recycled as e-waste.
items.example: Do not put them in ordinary rubbish.

mistakes.text: A coil is a magnet only while current flows. Switch it off and the magnetism stops.
A voltaic cell needs two different metals. Two pieces of the same metal will not work.
Galvani’s frog was not the source of the electricity. It came from the metals and the liquid.
Dry cells are easier to carry than voltaic cells, not harder.
